m-ZEH-eh mah-SAHN-jah.

Of course, you may ask, kah-BOO-lah.

I usually hear the sound coming from the Mosque early in the morning, What does that sound mean?
m-ZEH-eh mah-SAHN-jah.
That’s a good question, kah-BOO-lah.
That sound is called ah-DHAH-nah.
For us Muslims, when we hear the ah-DHAH-nah, we prepare and go to the Mosque to pray.
kah-BOO-lah.
Oh! So, the ah-DHAH-nah is like the bell that rings at the church?
m-ZEH-eh mah-SAHN-jah.
Yes, kah-BOO-lah.
In Churches, they use a bell, and in the Mosque, we use the ah-DHAH-nah to remind people that it is time for prayers.

Tanzania has different types of traditional houses such as m-SOHN-geh, BAHN-dah and TEM-beh.
m-SOHN-geh house
m-SOHN-geh house is a type of house built with a pointed top.
Some Tanzanian communities that use these houses include the wah-HAH-yah, wah-SAH-fwah, wafipa, wah-CHAH-gah, Waha and wah-NYAHM-boh.

BAHN-dah house
BAHN-dah house is a type of house with a two-sided roof.
Some Tanzanian communities that use these houses include the wah-nyah-MWEH-zee, wah-soo-KOO-mah, wah-nyah-KYOO-sah and wah-MWEH-rah.
A traditional BAHN-dah house made of bamboo walls and a thick grass roof.

TEM-beh house
TEM-beh house is a type of house with a flat roof covered with grass and mud.
Tanzanian communities that use these houses include the wah-GOH-goh, wah-nyah-TOO-roo, wah-nyee-RAHM-bah, wah-sahn-DAH-weh and wah-nyee-SAHN-zoo.

n-CHEE yenye mali nyingi, na wanyama kwa mamia,
Nenda na huko ziwani, na sah-MAH-kee pokelewe,
Huo oo-tah-JEE-ree wapi, uwe makini kusema,
oo-foo-KAH-rah umetanda, ndiyo maana sielewi.
oo-tah-JEE-ree kwetu pambo, mapato tunakusanya,
n-CHEE kavu twasafiri, baharini meli zetu,
too-oon-GAH-neh kwa pamoja, kuwapinga wahujumu,
too-wah-keh-MEH-eh wakija, warudisha gurudumu,
oo-tah-JEE-ree mwaujua, wa n-CHEE yetu hazina,
Daima nitaipenda, n-CHEE yangu Tanzania.

mah-WEHN-zee was crying.

mah-WEHN-zee replied, I had two one thousand shillings, one to buy flour and the other to buy vegetables.
